ఏతేన పూజావిధినా మాసాన్ ద్వాదశ హాయనమ్।  
నీత్వా చోపరమేత్ సాధ్వీ కార్తికే చరమేఽహని॥౬-౧౯-౨౧॥  
శ్వో భూతేఽప ఉపస్పృశ్య కృష్ణమభ్యర్చ్య పూర్వవత్। పయఃశృృతేన జుహుయాచ్చరుణా సహ సర్పిషా।  
పాకయజ్ఞవిధానేన ద్వాదశైవాహుతీః పతిః॥౬-౧౯-౨౨॥  
---శ్రీమద్భాగవతే మహాపురాణే

307fc0c840.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in uttarāṣāḍhā makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′01.83″.
307fc0c840.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′01.83″, 0°40′56.97″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°06′36.48″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.17, elongation 16°01′11.43″ E). budhaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°47′38.30″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -0.85, elongation 16°04′48.31″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

Masterda Surya Sen (along with colleague Tarakeswar Dastidar) was killed by British (after severe torture) on this day. He led a group of revolutionaries on 18 April 1930 to raid the armoury of police and auxiliary forces from the Chittagong armoury - sadly that had failed.

While hiding, Netra Sen informed the British of his hiding place, and the police came and captured him in February 1933. Before Netra Sen could be rewarded by the British, a revolutionary came into his house and beheaded him with da (a long knife). As Netra Sen's wife was a big supporter of Surya Sen, she never disclosed the name of the revolutionary who killed Netra Sen.

3158cea7ad.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śaniḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′54.44″.
3158cea7ad.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′54.44″, 0°33′44.12″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°40′20.83″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.13, elongation 10°14′15.62″ W). śaniḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°14′15.27″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.70, elongation 10°20′38.14″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

3179ee624d.b: Total lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (mukha/ascending).
3179ee624d.d: Umbral magnitude: 1.36 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:14►02:25 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra śatabhiṣak/pūrvaprōṣṭhapadā/uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or punarvasuḥ (anujanma) or viśākhā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: kumbhaḥ, mīnaḥ, karkaṭaḥ, vr̥śchikaḥ get more ashubha phala, mithunam, siṁhaḥ, tulā, makaraḥ somewhat ashubha, mēṣaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ, kanyā, dhanuḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
3179ee624d.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

317fbfe66f.b: Event occured on 1746-03-21 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
317fbfe66f.d:
ChoTTa ghallUghAra massacre of sikhs began on 3 Jeth 1746 with the rounding up and massacre of Sikh inhabitants of Lahore. An estimated 7,000 Sikhs were massacred in total.

The operation was planned and executed by Lakhpat Rai, who was a Revenue Minister in the Court of Lahore to avenge the killing of his brother, Jaspat Rai, a military commander by the Sikhs earlier in the same year.

31e93b8143.d: Preceptor Śrī Chandraśekharendra having remained in the Pīṭha for thirty-seven years attained Siddhi on Kṛṣṇadvitīya of Puṣya month in the year Subhakṛt. Śrī Maṭha moved to Kumbhaghona town during the period of this ācārya; his siddhi was also in Kumbhaghona. Śivāṣṭapadī, a lyrical work on the model of Gitagovinda of Śrī Jayadeva was composed only by this ācārya. His siddhi was during Śalivahana era 1705. The adhishthanam is located at https://maps.app.goo.gl/Zrry6C2Sbqd3NUAS6, in the premises of the Kumbhaghonam Kanchi Shankara Matham.
31e93b8143.s:

ఇతిహాసగర్భగూఢనామధామాదిపూర్వకః॥౮॥  
అనామ సర్వనామైతద్ బ్రహ్మేతీవ ప్రదర్శయన్।  
జయత్యభయదశ్చన్ద్రశేఖరేన్ద్రో యతీశ్వరః॥౯॥  
శ్రీమఠం కుమ్భఘోణం యోఽనయన్నయవిద్ ఆత్మవాన్।  
తత్రైవ సంస్థితో యత్ర మఠోఽబ్దద్విశతీం స్థితః॥౧౦॥  
శ్రీచన్ద్రశేఖరేన్ద్రః సప్తత్రింశత్సమాః స్థితః పీఠే।  
శుభకృతి పుష్యే కృష్ణద్వితీయతిథ్యామ్ ఇయాయ కైవల్యమ్॥౧౧॥

3202697eb2.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′13.10″.
3202697eb2.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′13.10″, 0°59′03.44″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′46.54″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.21″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′33.44″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.68″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

3234b367dc.d:
Varagur, nestled on the banks of the Kudamurutti River (kuḍamuruṭṭi), a tributary of the Kaveri, is a quaint village steeped in spiritual heritage. It is renowned for its connection with the revered Narayana Theertha Swamigal, the composer of Krishna Leela Tharangini, who achieved Deva Mukthi here following the Vishvarupa Darshan of Shri Venkatesha Perumal. This village, initially known as Bhoopathi Rajapuram and located in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu, India, is often referred to as “Heaven on Earth” (Bhoolaka Vaikuntam). With a history spanning over a thousand years, Varagur's picturesque main street starts from the Kathungalaaru brook and is adorned with significant temples, including the Pillayar temple with its pond, the Maha Kailasanatha Kovil (https://maps.app.goo.gl/mqDK3jqVD5DZfZ5u5), and the prominent Sri Venkatesa Perumal Kovil (https://maps.app.goo.gl/LkiXdeUoB1YUpxCf6).

The village's principal deity, Sri Venkatesa Perumal, originally installed as Sri Lakshmi Narayana by Paranthaka Chola, known as Veera Narayanan, represents a pinnacle of Chola period architecture. The arrival of Sri Narayana Theertha Swamigal from Andhra Pradesh, who sought blessings from Sri Venkatesa Perumal, marked a significant chapter in the village's history, leading to its renaming as Varahapuri, and eventually, Varagur. Varagur's cultural calendar is highlighted by the Uriyadi Utsavam, a grand festival commencing on Gayathri Japam Day, the day after Avani Avittam, and spanning ten days up to the day after Janmashtami.

A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

32e95c41b1.d:
On this day, Tawang was securely integrated into India by the efforts of Major Khathing, deputed by governor of Assam, Jairamdas Daulatram.

Context
In Jan 1951, then-the governor of Assam, Jairamdas Daulatram summoned Major Khathing and entrusted him with a top-secret mission: 'To go and integrate Tawang into India'. Major Khathing afterwards transferred on deputation as an assistant political officer, to the Indian Frontier Administrative Service. (to maintain the secrecy of the mission).

Major Khathing put together a team of two companies. After several days of travel, Major Khathing and his team moved to Tawang via the Jang and Sela mountain pass. The forces reached Tawang on the 7th of February, 1951. Major Khathing summoned Tibetan officials for the meeting. They were then given notice that any representatives of the Tibetan government will no longer have jurisdiction over people living south of the Bumla range. In the following days after that, all the officials of the 11 Tibetan Administrative Units were directed not to take any further orders from Tibetan officials. (Tibet was under China's control by then)

Tibetan officials asked for time to get permission from Lhasa. However, Major Khathing realized the crucial importance of time and rejected the request citing the Simla Treaty of 1914, according to which the area belonged to the GOI. From that day after, 11th of Feb 1951, Tawang became a part of India. Some historians believe that the incident was the initiative of the Assam Governor and PM Nehru was in a blackout for the whole time. Others are of opinion that PM was aware of the incident.

32fb51e0fb.d: Last three days of māgha-māsaḥ are especially sacred. By means of baths in Māgha, calamities perish. By means of baths in Māgha sins perish. Māgha is superior to all sacrifices, and gives the fruit of (all kinds of) charity. Māgha roars (louder) than sacrifices. Māgha roars (louder) than yōga. And O vidyādhara, Māgha roars (louder) than severe penance. The fruit which men obtain by (observing) restraints for ten years at Puṣkara, Kurukṣetra, Brahmāvarta having profuse water, at Avimukta, Prayāga, confluence of Gaṅgā and the ocean, is obtained by bathing for three days in Māgha! There is no doubt! Those, in whose mind there is, for a long time, interest in heaven, should bathe in water anywhere when the Sun is in makara. Those who desire to have qualities like (long) life, (good) health, wealth, handsomeness, good fortune, should not give up bathing in Māgha. So also those who are afraid of hell, of poverty that is heaped, should by all means bathe in the month of Māgha. O best king, for washing off the mud of poverty, sins and bad luck, there is no other remedy than a bath in Māgha. Acts done without faith give small fruits. (But) a bath in Māgha gives the entire fruit. He who, with or without a desire, bathes anywhere outside (his house) in water, does not have sorrows in this or in the next world. As in the two fortnights the Moon waxes and wanes, in the same way in Māgha sins decrease and the heap of religious merit increases. As various gems come up from a mine, so religious merit of men springs up due to a bath in Māgha. As the desire-yielding cow fulfils the desire, or the desire-yielding gem gives the desired object, so a bath in Māgha fulfils all desires in the world. Penance is the best in Kṛtayuga, knowledge in Tretā-yuga, sacrifice in Dvāpara, knowledge (devotion?) in Kaliyuga, and Māgha in all the ages. The bath in Māgha, O king, showers with the streams of merit all the varṇas and the stages of life. (Translation: https://www.wisdomlib.org/hinduism/book/the-padma-purana/d/doc365704.html)
32fb51e0fb.s:
భృగురువాచ---  
మాఘస్నానైర్విపన్నాశో మాఘస్నానైరఘక్షయః।  
సర్వవ్రతాధికో మాఘః సర్వదానఫలప్రదః॥౬౭॥  
మాఘో గర్జతి యజ్ఞేభ్యో మాఘో యోగాచ్చ గర్జతి।  
తీవ్రాచ్చ తపసో మాఘో భో విద్యాధర గర్జతి॥౬౮॥  
పుష్కరే చ కురుక్షేత్రే బ్రహ్మావర్తే పృథూదకే।  
అవిముక్తే ప్రయాగే చ గఙ్గాసాగరసఙ్గమే॥౬౯॥  
యత్ఫలం దశభిర్వర్షైః ప్రాప్యతే నియమైర్నరైః।  
తత్ఫలం ప్రాప్యతే మాఘే త్ర్యహస్నానాన్న సంశయః॥౭౦॥  
స్వర్గభోగే చిరం వాసో యేషాం మనసి వర్తతే।  
యత్ర క్వాపి జలే తైస్తు స్నాతవ్యం మృగభాస్కరే॥౭౧॥  
ఆయురారోగ్యసమ్పత్తౌ రూపే సుభగతా గుణే।  
యేషాం మనోరథస్తైస్తు స్నాతవ్యం మృగభాస్కరే॥   
యే తు బిభ్యతి నరకాద్ దారిద్యాబ్ధేస్త్రసన్తి యే।  
సర్వథా తైః ప్రయత్నేన స్నాతవ్యం మృగభాస్కరే॥౭౩॥  
దారిద్ర్యపాపదౌర్భాగ్యపఙ్కప్రక్షాలనాయ వై।  
మాఘస్నానాన్న చాన్యోఽస్తి హ్యుపాయః సురసత్తమ॥౭౪॥   
శ్రద్ధాహీనాని కర్మాణి కృతాన్యల్పఫలాని వై।  
ఫలం దదాతి సమ్పూర్ణం మాఘస్నానం యథావిధి॥౭౫॥  
అకామో వా సకామో వా యత్ర క్వాపి బహిర్జలే।  
ఇహాముత్ర చ దుఃఖాని మాఘస్నాయీ న పశ్యతి॥౭౬॥  
పక్షద్వయే యథా చన్ద్రః క్షీయతే వర్ధతే తథా।  
పాతకం క్షీయతే మాఘే పుణ్యరాశిర్వివర్ధతే॥౭౭॥  
యథాఽబ్ధౌ ఖలు జాయన్తే రత్నాని వివిధాని చ।  
ఆయుర్విత్తం కలత్రాదిసమ్పదో మాఘతస్తథా॥౭౮॥  
కామధేనుర్యథా కామం చిన్తామణిశ్చ చిన్తితమ్।  
మాఘస్నానం దదాతీహ తద్వత్సర్వమనోరథాన్॥౭౯॥   
కృతే తపః పరం జ్ఞానం త్రేతాయాం యజనం తథా।  
ద్వాపరే చ కలౌ దానం మాఘః సర్వయుగేషు చ॥౮౦॥   
సర్వేషాం సర్వవర్ణానామాశ్రమాణాం చ సర్వదా।   
మాఘస్నానం హి ధర్మస్య ధారాభిః ఖలు వర్షతి॥౮౧॥

333b0960ba.d: The eclipse is still in progress at moonset (grastAstamana). Umbral magnitude: 1.15 (parimāṇa ≈12.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 17:46►06:26 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. Falling on a Monday, this is an especially auspicious chūḍāmaṇi (crest-jewel) eclipse. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

333f84d0fa.d:
On this day, Taimur massacred about 100k Hindus in Loni which stood in the NE of Delhi.

Events (via MT)
On December 10th he proceed to attack the Loni that stood the north-east of Delhi, the Hindu defenders shaken by the loss of their chief failed to put an effective fight and were trashed by the Timurid army. Timur seized about 100,000 Hindus after the battle by encircling them in a crescent-like movement, even as their mass hunting expeditions on the steppe. He ordered his men to slaughter each one of them right away. He proudly describes how a Mullah who had not even killed a sparrow in the past now slew several Hindus with great enthusiasm. 

Context
Timur was on his way to wrest Delhi and India from the Tughlaqs, who had weakened.

33c956ed28.b: Event occured on 1700-10-12 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
33c956ed28.d:
On this day, fear of the Marathas grips Aurangzeb and he falls down and hurts his leg in the lavatory and remains lame for rest of his life continuing the legacy of his ancestor Taimurlang. (Muntakhabulubab of Khafi Khan, vol 2, page 476) The below account is from "History of Aurangzib [v5](https://archive.org/details/aurangzeb-1-2-jadunath-sarkar/Aurangzeb-5%20%28Jadunath%20Sarkar%29/page/131/mode/1up) ch 54, pg 138 by jAduNath sarkar.

> After five weeks' rest at Bhushangarh, the imperial camp was shifted (on 30th August 1700), to Khawaspur,(17.30 N. 75.1 E. on the Man river; 36 m. east of Bhushangarh, and 14 m. s. e. of Mhasvad.) 36 miles off, where food-stuffs and grass were abundant. Khawaspur stands on the left bank of the Man, a small waterless stream at that point. The tents of the army covered both its banks and even its dry bed, which in that season presented "only the mirage of water." But in the night of 1st October, while the men were fast asleep, a high flood caused by heavy and untimely rainfall on the hills, came suddenly sweeping through the river bed, overtopped its banks and spread over the plains beyond, "turning the land into one sheet of water." Many men and animals perished; many more, including even the nobles, were left absolutely poor and naked; nearly all the tents and property were damaged. Happily, the water went down early in the morning, otherwise "not one man would have survived." [M. A. 431, K. K. ii. 475.]
>
> When the flood first struck the camp, a little before midnight, and the tents began to fill with water, men tried to run to safety, but could see no path of escape in the darkness, only waves on all sides. A loud cry arose throughout the army. The Emperor was in his privy when this universal outcry reached his ears. Imagining that the Marathas had burst into the camp, he rose in alarm, but stumbled and dislocated his right knee. The doctors failed to set it properly, and he remained a little lame for the rest of his life. (He took his bath of recovery, on leaving the sick-bed, on 30th November. [Akhbarat.]) The Court flatterers used to console him by saying that it was the heritage of his ancestor Timur the Lame and a token that he would repeat the victories and success of that world-conqueror! [K. K. 476, Storia, 255, Dil. ii. 134a.]

On this day, Awrangzeb learned about his officer's attempt to capture a bairAgI and his idols and its failure thanks to rAjaputra action.

News record
The Emperor learnt from a secret news-writer of Delhi that in Jaisinghpura, Bairagis used to worship idols, and that the Censor on hearing of it had gone there, arrested Sri Krishna Bairagi and taken him with 15 idols away to his house; then the Rajputs had assembled, flocked to the Censor’s house, wounded three footmen of the Censor and tried to seize the Censor himself so that the latter set the Bairagi free and sent the copper idols to the local subahdar.

344a139dc2.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between guruḥ and śukraḥ in maghā siṁhaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°29′42.13″.
344a139dc2.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°29′42.13″, 0°29′22.24″ apart, disc-to-disc. guruḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 0°54′57.39″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.70, elongation 3°59′23.23″ E). śukraḥ at maghā-4 siṁhaḥ (latitude 1°24′39.52″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 4°07′52.87″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śukraḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) guruḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
344a139dc2.s:
భావాభావాయ లోకానాం కల్పనేయం ప్రదర్శితా।  
స్వమార్గగాః ప్రయాన్త్యేతే దూరమన్యోన్యమాశ్రితాః॥  
--సూర్యసిద్ధాన్తే  
  
షణ్మాసం గ్రహభిన్నభం త్యజ శుభే యౌద్ధం తథోత్పాతభమ్।  
--ముహూర్తచిన్తామణౌ (నారదసంహితానుసారేణ)

344f16788b.s:
యః మాధవే వైశాఖమాసే, త్రయోదశీచతుర్దశీపూర్ణిమాసు తిథిషు స్నానాదికం కరోతి  
స నిశ్చయేన మోక్షం ప్రాప్నుయాత్। యథా పురా ధనశర్మా బ్రాహ్మణః త్రయః ప్రేతాశ్చ  
ముక్తిం ప్రాపురితి। అత్ర ప్రసిద్ధా కథా సప్తదశాధ్యాయాత్మకపాద్మోక్తవైశాఖమాహాత్మ్యే।  
పురా విష్ణునా త్రయోదశ్యాం హిరణ్యాక్షః, చతుర్దశ్యాం మధుశ్చ ఘాతితః,  
పౌర్ణమాస్యాం భూమ్యుద్ధారశ్చ కృతః, తతః ప్రభృతి తాస్తిథయః పుణ్యా జాతాః!  
శ్రుతదేవ ఉవాచ---  
యాస్తిస్రస్తిథయః పుణ్యా అన్తిమాః శుక్లపక్షకే।  
వైశాఖమాసి రాజేన్ద్ర పూర్ణిమాన్తాః శుభావహాః॥౧॥  
అన్త్యాః పుష్కరిణీసంజ్ఞాః సర్వపాపక్షయావహాః।  
మాధవే మాసి యః పూర్ణం స్నానం కర్తుం న చ క్షమః॥౨॥  
తిథిష్వేతాసు స స్నాయాత్పూర్ణమేవ ఫలం లభేత్।  
సర్వే దేవాస్త్రయోదశ్యాం స్థిత్వా జన్తూన్పునన్తి హి॥౩॥  
పూర్ణాయాః పర్వతీర్థైశ్చ విష్ణునా సహ సంస్థితాః।  
చతుర్దశ్యాం సయజ్ఞాశ్చ దేవా ఏతాన్పునన్తి హి॥౪॥  
బ్రహ్మఘ్నం వా సురాపం వా సర్వానేతాన్పునన్తి హి।  
ఏకాదశ్యాం పురా జజ్ఞే వైశాఖ్యామమృతం శుభమ్॥౫॥  
ద్వాదశ్యాం పాలితం తచ్చ విష్ణునా ప్రభవిష్ణునా।  
త్రయోదశ్యాం సుధాం దేవాన్పాయయామాస వై హరిః॥౬॥  
జఘాన చ చతుర్దశ్యాం దైత్యాన్దేవవిరోధినః।  
పూర్ణాయాం సర్వదేవానాం సామ్రాజ్యాప్తిర్బభూవ హ॥౭॥  
తతో దేవాః సుసన్తుష్టా ఏతాసాం చ వరం దదుః।  
తిసృణాం చ తిథీనాం వై ప్రీత్యోత్ఫుల్లవిలోచనాః॥౮॥  
ఏతా వైశాఖమాసస్య తిస్రశ్చ తిథయః శుభాః।  
పుత్రపౌత్రాదిఫలదా నరాణాం పాపహానిదాః॥౯॥  
యోఽస్మిన్మాసే చ సమ్పూర్ణే న స్నాతో మనుజాధమః।  
తిథిత్రయే తు స స్నాత్వా పూర్ణమేవ ఫలం లభేత్॥౧౦॥  
తిథిత్రయేఽప్యకుర్వాణః స్నానదానాదికం నరః।  
చాణ్డాలీం యోనిమాసాద్య పశ్చాద్రౌరవమశ్నుతే॥౧౧॥  
ఉష్ణోదకేన యః స్నాతి మాధవే చ తిథిత్రయే।  
రౌరవం నరకం యాతి యావదిన్ద్రాశ్చతుర్దశ॥౧౨॥  
పితౄన్దేవాన్సముద్దిశ్య దధ్యన్నం న దదాతి యః।  
పైశాచీం యోనిమాసాద్య తిష్ఠత్యాభూతసమ్ప్లవమ్॥౧౩॥  
ప్రవృత్తానాం చ కామానాం మాధవే నియమే కృతే।  
అవశ్యం విష్ణుసాయుజ్యం యుజ్యతే నాత్ర సంశయః॥౧౪॥  
ఆమాసం నియమాసక్తః కుర్యాద్యది దినత్రయే।  
తేన పూర్ణఫలం ప్రాప్య మోదతే విష్ణుమన్దిరే॥౧౫॥  
యో వై దేవాన్పితౄన్విష్ణుం గురుముద్దిశ్య మానవః।  
న స్నానాది కరోత్యద్ధాఽముష్య శాపప్రదా వయమ్॥౧౬॥  
నిఃసన్తానో నిరాయుశ్చ నిఃశ్రేయస్కో భవేదితి।  
ఇతి దేవా వరం దత్త్వా స్వధామాని యయుః పురా॥౧౭॥  
తస్మాత్తిథిత్రయం పుణ్యం సర్వాఘౌఘవినాశనమ్।  
అన్త్యం పుష్కరిణీసంజ్ఞం పుత్రపౌత్రవివర్ధనమ్॥౧౮॥  
యా నారీ సుభగాఽపూపపాయసం పూర్ణిమాదినే।  
బ్రాహ్మణాయ సకృద్దద్యాత్కీర్తిమన్తం సుతం లభేత్॥౧౯॥  
గీతాపాఠం తు యః కుర్యాదన్తిమే చ దినత్రయే।  
దినేదినేఽశ్వమేధానాం ఫలమేతి న సంశయః॥౨౦॥  
సహస్రనామపఠనం యః కుర్య్యాచ్చ దినత్రయే।  
తస్య పుణ్యఫలం వక్తుం కః శక్తో దివి వా భువి॥౨౧॥  
సహస్రనామభిర్దేవం పూర్ణాయాం మధుసూదనమ్।  
పయసా స్నాప్య వై యాతి విష్ణులోకమకల్మషమ్॥౨౨॥  
సమస్తవిభవైర్యస్తు పూజయేన్మధుసూదనమ్।  
న తస్య లోకాః క్షీయన్తే యుగ కల్పాది వ్యత్యయే॥౨౩॥  
అస్నాత్వా చాప్యదత్త్వా చ వైశాఖశ్చ మతో యది।  
స బ్రహ్మహా గురుఘ్నశ్చ పితౄణాం ఘాతకస్తథా॥౨౪॥  
శ్లోకార్ధం శ్లోకపాదం వా నిత్యం భాగవతోద్భవమ్।  
వైశాఖే చ పఠన్మర్త్యో బ్రహ్మత్వం చోపపద్యతే॥౨౫॥  
యో వై భాగవతం శాస్త్రం శృణోత్యేతద్దినత్రయే।  
న పాపైర్లిప్యతే క్వాపి పద్మపత్రమివామ్భసా॥౨౬॥  
దేవత్వం మనుజైః ప్రాప్తం కైశ్చిత్సిద్ధత్వమేవ చ।  
కైశ్చిత్ప్రాప్తో బ్రహ్మభావో దినత్రయనిషేవణాత్॥౨౭॥  
బ్రహ్మజ్ఞానేన వై ముక్తిః ప్రయాగమరణేన వా।  
అథవా మాసి వైశాఖే నియమేన జలాప్లుతేః॥౨౮॥  
నీలవృషం సముత్సృజ్య వైశాఖ్యాం చ జలాప్లుతేః।  
సమస్తబన్ధనిర్ముక్తః పుమాన్యాతి పరం పదమ్॥౨౯॥  
గాం సవత్సాం ద్విజేన్ద్రాయ సీదతే చ కుటుమ్బినే।  
ఇహాపమృత్యునిర్ముక్తః పరత్ర చ పరం వ్రజేత్॥౩౦॥  
స్నానదానవిహీనస్తు వైశాఖీ చైవ యో నయేత్।  
శ్వానయోనిశతం ప్రాప్య విష్ఠాయాం జాయతే కృమిః॥౩౧॥  
తిస్రః కోట్యోఽర్ధకోటిశ్చ తీర్థాని భువనత్రయే।  
సమ్భూయ మన్త్రయాఞ్చక్రుః పాపసఙ్ఘాతశఙ్కితాః॥౩౨॥  
జనా అస్మాసు పాపిష్ఠా విసృజన్తి స్వకం మలమ్।  
తదస్మాకం కథం గచ్ఛేదితి చిన్తాసమన్వితాః॥౩౩॥  
తీర్థపాదం హరిం జగ్ముః శరణ్యం శరణం విభుమ్।  
స్తుత్వా చ బహుభిః స్తోత్రైః ప్రార్థయామాసురఞ్జసా॥౩౪॥  
దేవదేవ జగన్నాథ సర్వాఘౌఘవినాశన।  
జనా అస్మాసు పాపిష్ఠాః స్నాత్వా పాపాని సర్వశః॥౩౫॥  
విసృజ్య త్వత్పదం యాన్తి త్వదాజ్ఞాధారిణో భువి।  
అస్మాకం చైవ తత్పాపం కథం గచ్ఛేజ్జనార్దన॥౩౬॥  
తదుపాయం వదాస్మాకం త్వత్పాదశరణైషిణామ్।  
ఇతి తీర్థైః ప్రార్థితస్తు భగవాన్భూతభావనః॥౩౭॥  
ప్రహసన్ప్రాహ తీర్థాని మేఘగమ్భీరయా గిరా।  
శ్రీభగవానువాచ---  
సితే పక్షే మేషసూర్యే వైశాఖాన్తేదినత్రయే॥౩౮॥  
సర్వతీర్థమయే పుణ్యే మమాపి ప్రాణవల్లభే।  
యూయం భగోదయాత్పూర్వం బహిఃసంస్థజలాప్లుతాః॥౩౯॥  
విముక్తాఘాః పుణ్యరూపా భవన్త్వాశు సునిర్మలాః।  
భవద్భిశ్చ విముక్తాఘైర్యే న స్నాతా దినత్రయే॥౪౦॥  
తేషు తిష్ఠన్తు తత్పాపం జనైర్యుష్మద్విరేచితమ్।  
ఇతి తీర్థపదో విష్ణుస్తీర్థానాం చ వరం దదౌ॥౪౧॥  
అనుజ్ఞాప్య చ తాన్యోగాత్తత్రైవాన్తరధీయత।  
స్వధామాని పునః ప్రాప్య తాని తీర్థాని నిత్యశః॥౪౨॥  
ప్రతివర్షం తు వైశాఖే తథైవాన్త్యదినత్రయే।  
తేనాఘౌఘం విముచ్యైవ యాన్తి నిర్మలతామహో॥౪౩॥  
యే తు స్నానం న కుర్వన్తి వైశాఖాన్తదినత్రయే।  
తే భవన్తు సమస్తానాం జనానాం పాతకాశ్రయాః॥౪౪॥  
ఇతి శాపం చ తీర్థాని హ్యస్నాతానాం వదన్తి చ।  
న తేన సదృశః పాపో యో న స్నాతో దినత్రయే॥౪౫॥  
విచారితేషు శాస్త్రేషు న దృష్టో న చ వై శ్రుతః।  
తస్మాద్దినత్రయే కార్యం స్నానదానార్చనాదికమ్॥౪౬॥  
అన్యథా నరకం యాతి యావదిన్ద్రాశ్చతుర్దశ।  
ఇత్యేతత్సర్వమాఖ్యాతం శ్రుతకీర్తే మహామతే॥౪౭॥  
---స్కాన్ద-మహాపురాణే వైష్ణవఖణ్డే వైశాఖమాహాత్మ్యే పఞ్చవింశోఽధ్యాయః

34752f9033.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈2.6 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
34752f9033.d: Magnitude: 22% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈2.6 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 00:33►17:09 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

347bccdf57.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′14.69″.
347bccdf57.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′14.69″, 0°59′05.03″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′49.31″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.56″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′34.62″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.82″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

350d915631.d: Perform snana four ghatikas before sunrise (during aruṇodayaḥ, when the Moon is still up, on the full-moon days of āṣāḍha, kārttika, māgha and vaiśākha – hence the name ā-kā-mā-vai) bestows strength, beauty, fame, dharma, knowledge, happiness, fortitude and health.
350d915631.s:
ఉదయాత్ ప్రాక్ చతస్రస్తు నాడికా అరుణోదయః।  
తత్ర స్నానం ప్రశంసన్తి స హి పుణ్యతమః స్మృతః॥  
బలం రూపం యశో ధర్మం జ్ఞానమాయుః సుఖం ధృతిమ్।  
ఆరోగ్యం పరమాప్నోతి సమ్యక్ స్నానేన మానవః॥  
భవిష్యే---  
వైశాఖీ కార్తికీ మాఘీ హ్యాషాఢ్యప్యతిపుణ్యదాః।  
స్నానదానవిహీనా వై తాసు రౌరవగామినః॥  
కార్తిక్యాం తు విశేషేణ యోఽభిగచ్ఛతి పుష్కరమ్ ।  
`ఫలం తత్రాక్షయం తేన లభతే భరతర్షభ'॥౩-౮౦-౩౨॥  
యస్తు వర్షశతం పూర్ణమగ్నిహోత్రముపాసతే ।  
కార్తికీం వా వసేదేకాం పుష్కరే సమమేవ తత్॥౩-౮౦-౩౭॥  
సరస్వత్యాం మహారాజ శతం సంవత్సరం చ తే ।  
దృశ్యన్తే భరతశ్రేష్ఠ వృత్తాం వై కార్తికీం సదా॥౩-౮౦-౧౧౫॥  
---మహాభారతే (కుమ్భఘోణ-సంస్కరణమ్)  
+++(Mahābhārata: Puṣkara on the Kārttikī; bathing at Śaśayāna on the Sarasvatī when the Kārttikī comes)+++

35b8230bd3.d:
On this Friday, crazed Muslim mobs desecrated and burned the temple of Bhagyalakshmi at Charminar in Hyderabad - They broke the main Murti of Lakshmi. The riots went on for 10 days and the shops of Marwadis were destroyed.

Background
In 1979, dramatic events shook the Muslim world: revolution in Iran at the hands of Imam Khomeini, the occupation of Afghanistan by the Soviet Army, while in Mecca a commando of fanatics wreaked havoc at the Muslim holy site. Salahuddin Owaisi of AIMIM called for a Bandh in Hyderabad, even when India had nothing to do with it. 

Aftermath
The riots stopped only after Saudi Arabia regained control of Grand Mosque in Mecca.  
After the riots, the Congress Government led by then CM Chenna Reddy did not take ANY action against MIM rioters.

35d4e3884f.d:
On this day, 1,461 Sikh soldiers of the Sikh regimental centre (1,050 of them raw recruits) at Ramgarh camp in the erstwhile Bihar state rebelled and murdered their commander, Brigadier RS Puri. The leaders of the mutiny divided the troops into two groups just outside of Banaras to avoid a rumoured roadblock.

Context
Many Sikh armymen were indoctrinated by Khalistanis. Fifteen percent of the Indian Army - including some of its most elite divisions - were composed of Sikhs. (But Sikhs were less than 2 percent of the population.) One of the bodies removed from Bhindranwale's basement command was that retired Maj. Gen. Shuhbeg Singh. He dismissed one day before getting his retirement. After his dismissal he joined the Khalistan movement as a military adviser. A couple of Sikh bodyguards later killed the prime minister Indira Gandhi.

The mutiny was sparked by an army assault the previous week on the holiest shrine of the Sikhs, the Golden Temple. Incidentally, the two top generals in the chain of command, Lt Gen RS Dayal MVC and Maj Gen KS Brar were Sikhs with distinguished records for service and gallantry.

Aftermath
Two other senior officers and a number of soldiers were seriously wounded in heavy shooting at the camp that began before noon and continued until 4 pm. The soldiers joined other angry Sikhs in hijacking private buses and trucks at gunpoint. 

One half was engaged by army artillery at Shakteshgarh railway station; those who managed to escape were rounded up by 21st Mechanised Infantry Regiment. The other half engaged with the artillery and troops of 20th Infantry Brigade, during which 35 soldiers (both sides) were killed. Sikh soldiers remaining behind at the camp raised a white flag of surrender when the reinforcements arrived.

Overall (including other incidents), about 5k Sikhs had mutinied. Many mutineers were court-martialed and dismissed. The Sikh Regiment's 9th battalion was disbanded. Some were retained, but soldiers from those battalions were made to wear a black band around their turbans to signify they had once betrayed the country.

366bfc5071.d: Aradhana Day of Govinda Damodara Swamigal. Sri Angarai Periyava (1992 sanyasa name “Ramachandrashraya”, also called Govinda Damodara Swamigal and Triplicane/Tiruvallikeni Periyava) was born Sri Kalyanarama Sastrigal (Bhagavathar) of Angarai village near Tiruchi. On the advice of the Kanchi Paramacharya (Mahaperiyava), he gave up his Indian Postal Department job despite having a large family to support, and devoted himself to the “Bhagavatha jeevanam” — performing seven-day Saptaha Parayanam recitals of the Srimad Bhagavatam and Bhattadri's Narayaneeyam with evening Tamil discourses, which he did before Janmashtami every year from 1973 to 1991 in the Paramacharya's presence. Renowned for extreme humility, simplicity and devotion to Rama and Guruvayurappan, he shunned all publicity, refused large audiences, and lived quietly for most of his life on Hanumantharayan Koil Street in Triplicane near the Parthasarathi temple. Mahaperiyava's own purvashrama younger brother “Sivan Sir” sent devotees to him for counsel. His adhishtanam is at Pazhur (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Jqu5xvrJXhV1HP3p9). He attained siddhi in 2004. Shri Ganapathy has written a beautiful article about Swamigal, on how He led His life as mentioned in Ramayanam (http://valmikiramayanam.in/wordpress/svkr.pdf).

36726b9637.s:

బ్రహ్మవైవర్తే---  
అప్రాప్తే భాస్కరే కన్యాం శేషభూతైత్రిభిర్దినైః।  
అర్ఘం దద్యురగస్త్యాయ గౌడదేశనివాసినః॥  
నారసింహే---  
శఙ్ఖే తోయం వినిక్షిప్య సితపుష్పాక్షతైర్యుతమ్।  
మన్త్రేణానేన వై దద్యాద్ దక్షిణాభిముఖః స్థితః॥  
అనేన ‘శఙ్ఖం పుష్పం ఫలం తోయమ్’ ఇత్యాది మన్త్రేణ। అత్ర దినత్రయే మన్త్రత్రయం యథా---  
కుమ్భయోనిసముత్పన్న మునీనాం మునిసత్తమ।  
ఉదయం తే లఙ్కాద్వారేఽర్ఘోఽయం ప్రతిగృహ్యతామ్॥౧॥  
శఙ్ఖం పుష్పం ఫలం తోయం రత్నాని వివిధాని చ।  
ఉదయం తే లఙ్కాద్వారేఽర్ఘోఽయం ప్రతిగృహ్యతామ్॥౨॥  
కాశపుష్పప్రతీకాశ వహ్నిమారుతసమ్భవ।  
ఉదయం తే లఙ్కాద్వారేఽర్ఘోఽయం ప్రతిగృహ్యతామ్॥౩॥  
ఇతి కేచిత్। రసమాలాయాం తు ప్రథమదినే తృతీయమన్త్రః, ద్వితీయే-ప్రథమమన్త్రః ఇతి భేదః।

3677e583a9.b: Partial solar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈2.0 of 12 aṅgulas), Sun at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
3677e583a9.d: Magnitude: 17% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈2.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 22:52►14:23 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā/maghā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or jyēṣṭhā (anujanma) or rēvatī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

36a0bcf9eb.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and budhaḥ in uttarāṣāḍhā makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′01.08″.
36a0bcf9eb.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′01.08″, 0°40′56.22″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°06′35.78″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.17, elongation 16°01′11.94″ E). budhaḥ at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°47′36.85″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -0.85, elongation 16°04′48.78″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

376e3c44bf.d: As per the saying “gurum prakāshayed dhīmān”, Shri Jayendra Sarasvati Shricharana installed the vigraha of Shri Bhagavatpada in all the Jyotirlinga Kshetras that He had extolled. Further He installed the divine form of Shri Bhagavatpada, the Jagadguru, in the four extremes of Bhārat—Jagannatha, Kanyakumari, Gokarna seashores and Kailasa—facing the respective directions. As per the wishes of His Guru Shri Chandrashekharendra Sarasvati Shricharana, He consoled the Sanatanis of the Kashmira Desha driven away from there, and took up laukika/vaidika efforts for their welfare. Even in the North-East end of Bharat, He likewise did pratishtha of Shri Bhagavatpada and conducted laukika/vaidika dharma-s so that difficulty should not befall Sanatana Dharma. He attained siddhi on Kumbha Phalguna Shukla Trayodashi in Hemalamba year in the forenoon (2018-02-28). The adhishthanam is in the premises of Kanchi Matham at https://maps.app.goo.gl/GqcNJ87GrkU2o4RB9.

3803d661b2.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śaniḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′54.56″.
3803d661b2.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′54.56″, 0°33′44.24″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°40′20.68″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.13, elongation 10°14′15.60″ W). śaniḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°14′15.25″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.70, elongation 10°20′38.15″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

388aa1d4b0.b: Observed on Amāvāsyā tithi of every (lunar) month (Sāṅgavaḥ/paraviddha).
388aa1d4b0.d: Anadhyayana on account of amāvāsyā. Several tithis in a month are nitya-anadhyayana days, including prathamā, aṣṭamī, chaturdaśī, amāvāsyā and pūrṇimā. Manu has said that performing adhyayana on these days destroys the Guru (Amavasya), Shishya (Chaturdashi) and the vīrya of the brahma (vēda) itself (Ashtami/Purnima). Similarly, Jabali Rishi has said that Adhyayana on prathama hurts the buddhi while adhyayana on chaturdaśī hurts the brahma (vēda) itself!
388aa1d4b0.s:
హారీతః—  
ప్రతిపత్సు చతుర్దశ్యామష్టమ్యాం పర్వణోర్ద్వయోః।  
శ్వోఽనధ్యాయేఽద్య శర్వర్యాం నాధీయీత కదాచన॥  
మనుః—  
అమావాస్యా గురుం హన్తి శిష్యం హన్తి చతుర్దశీ।  
బ్రహ్మాష్టకాపౌర్ణమాస్యస్తస్మాత్తాః పరివర్జయేదితి॥  
యాజ్ఞవల్క్యః—  
పఞ్చదశ్యాం చతుర్దశ్యాం అష్టమ్యాం రాహుసూతకే।

388c163ddf.b: Event occured on 1727-02-19 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
388c163ddf.d:
On Shivaratri day, Feb 8th 1727, Siddi sAt, launched a Jihad to attack the Rama temple on the Chiplun hill (when brahmendra svAmI was absent).
Having desecrated the idols he rounded up several hundred brAhmaNas, tortured them and killed many of them. 

Context
Svami Brahmendra had built a large temple of the bhArgava on hill near
Chiplun, which was lavishly endowed by the Hindus of the Maharatta
country.  
At this time the Siddi governor of Govalkot and Anjanvel, two fortified posts not far from the shrine, was one Siddi Sat, a competent, if rather rough, officer.  
In 1727, the Siddi admiral, Siddi sAt, launched a naval raid on
the adjacent territory of Govalkot and Anjanvel, annexed them and
fortified them for an offensive on the Hindus. The African imitator of
his Arab role-models was seized with an itch to become a Ghazi and be
recognized as a pre-eminent Moslem. 

This attack enraged the Hindus
who called upon Shahu to take the strongest action.

Aftermath
(The below is from New History of Marathas v2 by sArdesai.)  
This wanton and certainly premeditated violence by a Muslim on a centre of Brahman orthodoxy, roused the whole of Maharashtra as if from a dream, and a cry for vengeance arose on all sides. The chief ruler of Janjira at once apologized for the foolish action of his subordinate, and restored whatever property was left intact. 

In a few days the Swami arrived on the spot, vented his wrath against the Siddi and left the place for good, having been granted another spot by Shahu up the Ghats at Dhavadsi near Satara, where he then erected new edifices and where an annual celebration for his deity is still held. 

The Swami appealed pathetically to Shahu and the icading Maratha commanders, calling upon then to wage a relentless holy war against the Siddi of Janjira. Time passed as no one was free to undertake the venture. When Bajirao returned victorious from his campaign of Dabhoi, both Shahu and the Swami became insistent on his punishing the Siddi for the unwarrantable crime he had committed.

392d54d782.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
392d54d782.s:
స్మృత్యన్తరే---  
అమా పాతశ్చ సఙ్క్రాన్తిస్తథా వైధృతిరేవ చ।  
అష్టకాశ్చైవ మన్వాదిర్యుగాదిశ్చ మహాలయః॥  
చన్ద్రసూర్యోపరాగశ్చ గజచ్ఛాయా తథైవ చ।  
ద్రవ్యబ్రాహ్మణసమ్పత్తిః శ్రాద్ధకాలాః ప్రకీర్తితాః॥  
మన్వన్తరాదయో మత్స్యపురాణే దర్శితాః---  
ఆశ్వయుక్ఛుక్లనవమీ కార్తికీ ద్వాదశీ సితా।  
తృతీయా చైత్రమాసస్య సితా భాద్రపదస్య చ॥  
ఫాల్గునస్యాప్యమావాస్యా పుష్యస్యైకాదశీ సితా।  
ఆషాఢస్యాపి దశమీ మాఘమాసస్య సప్తమీ॥  
శ్రావణస్యాష్టమీ కృష్ణా తథాఽఽషాఢీ చ పూర్ణిమా।  
కార్తికీ ఫాల్గునీ చైత్రీ జ్యైష్ఠీ పఞ్చదశీ సితా॥  
మన్వన్తరాదయశ్చైతే దత్తస్యాక్షయకారకాః।  
కృతం శ్రాద్ధం విధానేన మన్వాదిషు యుగాదిషు॥  
హాయనాని ద్విసాహస్రం పితౄణాం తృప్తిదం భవేత్।  
ఆసు స్నానం జపో హోమః పుణ్యానన్త్యాయ కల్పతే॥  
మహాభారతేఽపి---   
యా మన్వాద్యా యుగాద్యాశ్చ తిథయస్తాసు మానవః।  
స్నాత్వా భుక్త్వా చ దత్త్వా చ తదనన్తఫలం లభేత్॥  
కాలాదర్శేఽపి---  
మన్వాద్యాసు యుగాద్యాసు ప్రదత్తః సలిలాఞ్జలిః।  
సహస్రవార్షికీ తృప్తిం పితౄణామావహేత్ పరామ్॥  
ద్విసహస్రాబ్దికీ తృప్తిం కృతం శ్రాద్ధం యథావిధి।  
స్నానం దానం జపో హోమః పుణ్యానన్త్యాయ కల్పతే॥  
పురుషార్థచిన్తామణౌ మనుః---  
సహస్రగుణితం దానం భవేద్దత్తం యుగాదిషు।  
కర్మ శ్రాద్ధాదికం చైవ తథా మన్వన్తరాదిషు॥

3954a4f5e7.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śaniḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′54.28″.
3954a4f5e7.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′54.28″, 0°33′43.96″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°40′21.01″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.13, elongation 10°14′15.55″ W). śaniḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°14′15.29″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.70, elongation 10°20′38.03″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

399547991f.d:
The temple of Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy, which has been a center of devotion from ancient times, once fell into disrepair. It was later renovated by Chinna Tirumalacharya, the grandson of Sri Tallapaka Annamacharya, as evidenced by an inscription dated March 22nd, 1510 CE at the temple's entrance. Despite regaining its glory for several years, the temple again faced neglect in the 20th century.

In 1940, an Archaka named Sri Sundara Raja Swamy from Kanchi, inspired by a dream in which Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy appeared, took it upon himself to clean the temple premises and resume regular pujas. He conveyed his dream to the villagers, narrating how Shri Venkateshwara Swamy manifested in the dream and instructed him to restore the temple's former splendor (Past Vaibhavam) by conducting Deepa Naivedya Aaradhana, after which Bhagavan vanished from the dream. On July 11, 1940, which was Ashada Shukla Paksha Shashti, Sundara Raja Swamy conducted a special puja, marking the day the deity revealed his divine form to devotees. This event led the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams to initiate the annual "Sakshatkara Vaibhavotsavams."

"Sakshatkaram" refers to the deity's holy appearance or Darshan. The Sakshatkara Vaibhavotsavam is a three-day festival that includes the day of the deity’s appearance (Ashada Suddha Shasti) and the days immediately before and after. The first day of the celebration includes a procession of the deity, Sri Kalyana Venkateshwara Swamy, along with His consorts, on the Pedda Shesha Vahanam, from the temple to the Kalyana Mandapa, followed by Abhishekam and Unjal Seva in the evening. The second day features Hanumantha Vahana Seva, and the third day concludes with the Garuda Vahana Seva at night. These celebrations provide devotees the opportunity to witness the deity and receive blessings.

399f5511bc.d: Magnitude: 50% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈6.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 03:10►17:45 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). 39e9ba5f68.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°36′15.14″.
39e9ba5f68.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°36′15.14″, 0°36′01.72″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°15′32.27″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.71, elongation 25°42′14.43″ W). śukraḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°39′17.14″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.87, elongation 25°39′40.00″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

అఫాలలోచనో శమ్భుర్భగవాన్ బాదరాయణః॥  
అభ్ర-శ్యామః పిఙ్గ-జటా-బద్ధ-కలాపః  
ప్రాంశుర్దణ్డీ కృష్ణమృగ-త్వక్-పరిధానః।  
సర్వాన్ లోకాన్ పావయమానః కవి-ముఖ్యః  
పారాశర్యః పర్వ-సురూపం వివృణోతు॥  
వ్యాసం వసిష్ఠ-నప్తారం శక్తేః పౌత్రమకల్మషమ్।  
పరాశరాత్మజం వన్దే శుక-తాతం తపోనిధిమ్॥  
కృష్ణ-ద్వైపాయనం వ్యాసం సర్వ-భూత-హితే రతమ్।  
వేదాబ్జ-భాస్కరం వన్దే శమాది-నిలయం మునిమ్॥  
విశ్వరూపం చ విశ్వేశం విశ్వ-సత్తా-ప్రదం శివమ్।  
వేదయోనిమహం వన్దే వ్యాసం వేదార్థ-సిద్ధిదమ్॥  
జయతి పరాశరసూనుః  
సత్యవతీహృదయనన్దనో వ్యాసః।  
యస్యాస్యకమలగలితం  
వాఙ్మయమమృతం జగత్ పిబతి॥

3aabb23773.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śaniḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°33′54.79″.
3aabb23773.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°33′54.79″, 0°33′44.47″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°40′20.42″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.13, elongation 10°14′15.66″ W). śaniḥ at rēvatī-3 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°14′15.21″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.70, elongation 10°20′38.26″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

3ac3f77711.s:
స్మృత్యన్తరే---  
అమా పాతశ్చ సఙ్క్రాన్తిస్తథా వైధృతిరేవ చ।  
అష్టకాశ్చైవ మన్వాదిర్యుగాదిశ్చ మహాలయః॥  
చన్ద్రసూర్యోపరాగశ్చ గజచ్ఛాయా తథైవ చ।  
ద్రవ్యబ్రాహ్మణసమ్పత్తిః శ్రాద్ధకాలాః ప్రకీర్తితాః॥  
అథాష్టకాః। తాశ్చతస్రః మార్గశీర్షాదిమాసచతుష్టయాపరపక్షాష్టమ్యః - తథా చ శౌనకః---  
హేమన్తశిశిరయోశ్చతుర్ణామపరపక్షాణామష్టమీష్వష్టకాః ఇతి।  
అత్ర విశేషమాహ విష్ణుః---  
అష్టకాస్తిస్రోఽష్టమ్యోఽన్వష్టక్యాః పూర్వేద్యుః ప్రౌష్ఠపదే హేమన్తశిశిరయోరపరపక్షేషు ఇతి। అన్వష్టక్యాః - నవమ్యః, పూర్వేద్యుః - సప్తమ్యః।  
కాలాదర్శేఽపి---  
మార్గశీర్షే చ పౌషే చ మాఘే ప్రౌష్ఠే చ ఫాల్గునే।  
కృష్ణపక్షేషు పూర్వేద్యురన్వష్టక్యం తథాఽష్టమీ।  
ఇతి తిస్రోఽష్టకాస్తాసు శ్రాద్ధం కుర్వీత పార్వణమ్।  
ఆశ్వలాయనః---  
హేమన్తశిశిరర్త్వోస్తు చతుర్ణామపి సత్తమైః।  
సమర్థైరష్టకా కార్యా కృష్ణానామష్టమీషు చ।   
ఏకస్యాం హి త్వశక్తేన కార్యా గృహ్యస్య వర్త్మనా ఇతి।  
బోధాయనోఽపి---  
ఉపరిష్టాన్ మాఘ్యాః పౌర్ణమాస్యా అపరపక్షస్య సప్తమ్యామష్టమ్యాం నవమ్యామితి క్రియేతాపి వాఽష్టమ్యామేవ ఇతి।

3ad0c54753.b: Observed on Pūrvaphalgunī nakshatra of Mithunam (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
3ad0c54753.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Amaraneedi Nayanmar, a Vaisya from Pazhaiyaarai in the Chola Kingdom, was a prosperous trader and a devout follower of Bhagavan Shiva. Despite his wealth and involvement in worldly affairs, he remained deeply committed to serving Shiva Bhaktas (devotees of Bhagavan Shiva). He practiced the sacred ritual of Maaheswara Puja, which involved reverently welcoming and serving Shiva Bhaktas, believing that serving them was as important as worshipping Bhagavan Shiva himself.

Desiring to devote himself more fully to this service, Amaraneedi Nayanmar moved to Tirunallur with his family, where he built a Mutt for accommodating Shiva Bhaktas. His devotion caught Bhagavan Shiva’s attention, who decided to test and reveal Nayanmar's devotion to the world. Disguised as a Brahmachari, Bhagavan Shiva visited Nayanmar's Mutt and entrusted him with a Kowpeenam (loincloth), claiming it was precious. However, Bhagavan Shiva made the Kowpeenam disappear, leading to a situation where Amaraneedi Nayanmar couldn’t return it.

Despite Amaraneedi Nayanmar's attempts to offer other wealth as compensation, the Brahmachari insisted on a Kowpeenam of equal value. When all Amaraneedi Nayanmar’s wealth could not match the weight of the Brahmachari’s Kowpeenam, representing the Vedas and Shastras, Amaraneedi Nayanmar, in desperation, placed himself, his wife, and child on the scale, and declared, If my service to the Shiva Bhaktas has indeed been genuine and heartfelt, may this scale balance with the other.'' Instantly, equilibrium was achieved between the two scales. This demonstrated that the value of Amaraneediar's devoted and altruistic service to the devotees of Bhagavan Shiva was on par with the significance of Bhagavan Shiva's Kowpeenam.

Witnessing this, the people around were amazed, and the Brahmachari revealed his true form as Bhagavan Shiva, accompanied by Mother Parvati. They blessed Amaraneedi Nayanmar and his family for their sincere service and charity, granting them eternal residence in Shiva’s Abode. The balance they were weighed on transformed into a celestial vehicle, carrying them to the divine realm. This story exemplifies the profound spiritual merit of selfless service and devotion to the devotees of the divine.
3ad0c54753.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

3b1e92c07f.d:
On this day, the jihAdist gAzi army of maliq kafr, the general of Alla-ad-din Khalji, completed a campaign to destroy a beautiful temple at rAmeshvaram.

(Source of the below account is Amir Khusroo’s Tarikh-i-Allai.)

Events per Khusroo
Maliq Kafr heard that in Brahmastpuri (Near Rameshwaram) there was a golden idol, round which many elephants were stabled. The Maliq started on a night expedition against this place, and in the morning seized no less than two hundred and fifty elephants. 

He then determined on razing the beautiful temple to the ground. That temple was beauteous as the Paradise of Shaddad, the golden temple of Ram (Rameshwaram) where the hellish Hindus worshiped their gods. The roof was covered with rubies and emeralds,-in short, it was the holy place of the Hindus. The Maliq dug up the temple from its foundations without leaving anything, and made the heads of the Brahmans and other idol worshiper dance from their necks and fall to the ground at their feet. And blood of Hindus flowed in torrents. The stone idols called Ling Mahadeo, which had been a long time established at that place. They were copulating sex organs worshiped by the Kafir Hindus. Up to this time, the kick of the horse of Islam had not yet broken them. The Musalmans destroyed all the lings, and idols of Deo Narain (viShNu), and the other gods. Had these idols been able to move they would have jumped to the fort of Lanka. Had those sex organs had legs they would have run at fright of the Moslems. There was much fierce fighting with the Hindu Nayakas defending the land who were finally butchered. Much gold and valuable jewels fell into the hands of the Musalmans, who returned to the royal canopy, after executing their project of the holy Jihad on the 13th of Zi-l ka’da, 710 H. (April, 1311 A.D.). They destroyed all the temples at Birdhul (Near Madhurai), and plundered the public treasury.

Context per Khusroo
The tongue of the sword of the Khalifat of the era, which is the tongue of the flame of Islam, has imparted light to the entire pagan darkness of Hindustan by the illumination of its guidance. On one side an iron wall of royal swords has been raised before the Kafirs of Mongolia, the Magog-like Tatars, so that all of the Mongolian tribe, deserted by Allah, drew their feet within their skirts amongst the hills of Ghazni, and even their advance-arrows had not strength enough to reach into Sind which was conquered by the sword of Islam. On the other side so, much dust arose from the battered temple of Somnath that even the sea was not able to settle it. On the right hand and on the left hand the army of Islam has conquered Hindustan from sea to sea, and several capitals of the rulers of the Hindus, in which the worship of the fire and their devilish gods and had prevailed since the time of the Jinns, have all been demolished. All these impurities of infidelity have been cleansed by the Sultan Alla-ad-din’s destruction of idols and temples, beginning with his first Jihad against Devgir (Devagiri in Maharashtra). Now the flames of the light of the Shariat and the righteous Fatwa illuminate all these unholy Hindu lands, and places for the callers to Namaz occupy the high places and the and Namaz is read in mosques. Allah be praised!

3b1f23e345.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′13.88″.
3b1f23e345.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′13.88″, 0°59′04.22″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′47.89″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.32″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′34.00″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.68″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

3bcfcccbe5.d: On 17 June in Kotah-ki-Serai near the Phool Bagh of Gwalior, a squadron of the 8th (King's Royal Irish) Hussars, under Captain Heneage, fought the large Indian force commanded by Rani Lakshmibai, who was trying to leave the area. The 8th Hussars charged into the Indian force, slaughtering 5,000 Indian soldiers, including any Indian "over the age of 16". They took two guns and continued the charge right through the Phool Bagh encampment. In this engagement, according to an eyewitness account, Rani Lakshmibai put on a sowar's uniform and attacked one of the hussars; she was unhorsed and also wounded, probably by his sabre. Shortly afterwards, as she sat bleeding by the roadside, she recognised the soldier and fired at him with a pistol, whereupon he "dispatched the young lady with his carbine".

3c0778fed9.d: Born as the son of Kāmeśvara and Kamalāmbā of Kāñci, the one named Kupanna who having received the initiation and preceptorship with the name Mahādeva, conducted the lectures on Bhāṣya ably for twenty-one times in nine years rejoicingly, attained siddhi on the pratipad of black fortnight in the month of Āṣāḍha of the year Akṣaya. As He stayed ever in the Vyāsācala, He is known as Vyāsācala and the author of Vyāsācaliya and other works. He attained siddhi in Vyāsācala.

స్వమార్గగాః ప్రయాన్త్యేతే దూరమన్యోన్యమాశ్రితాః॥  
--సూర్యసిద్ధాన్తే  
  
షణ్మాసం గ్రహభిన్నభం త్యజ శుభే యౌద్ధం తథోత్పాతభమ్।  
--ముహూర్తచిన్తామణౌ (నారదసంహితానుసారేణ)

3c44d5cf9a.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′12.81″.
3c44d5cf9a.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′12.81″, 0°59′03.15″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′46.06″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.16″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′33.24″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.67″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

మౌంజీమేఖలయా యుక్తః కౌపీనపరిధారకః॥   
కైకేయీహస్తతః పిణ్డం జహార చిల్హిపక్షిణీ।  
గచ్ఛన్త్యాకాశమార్గేణ తదా వాయుర్మహానభూత్॥  
తుణ్డాత్ ప్రగలితే పిణ్డే వాయుర్నీత్వాఞ్జనాఞ్జలౌ।  
క్షిప్తవాన్ స్థాపితం పిణ్డం భక్షయామాస తత్క్షణాత్॥  
నవమాసగతే పుత్రం సుషువే సాఽఞ్జనా శుభమ్। (హనుమదుపాసనాకల్పద్రుమ)

న భవేత్ తస్య దారిద్ర్యం జన్మాన్తరశతేష్వపి॥

నక్తం భోక్ష్యామి దేవేశ త్రాహి మాం కృపయా హర॥  
మదనరత్న-నిర్ణయామృతాన్తర్గతస్కన్దపురాణవచనాని---  
యదా త్రయోదశీ శుక్లా మన్దవారేణ సంయుతా।  
ఆరబ్ధవ్యం వ్రతం తత్ర సన్తానఫలసిద్ధయే॥  
ఆయురారోగ్యసిద్ధ్యర్థం భానువారేణ సంయుతా।  
  
విశ్వం విష్ణూ రుద్ర విశ్వాధికోఽసి  
యజ్ఞో విష్ణుస్త్వం తు రాజాధ్వరాణామ్।  
శ్రీశస్వర్ణాద్రీ ఆత్మహస్తాగ్రసంస్థౌ  
శ్రీకణ్ఠోఽవ్యాద్ దేవతాబ్రాహ్మణోఽస్మాన్॥  
హాలాహలం హర నియమ్య పరానియామ్యం  
సర్వాన్ సురాన్ సపది యః స్వనతానరక్షత్।  
దృప్తానశిక్షత పునర్యుధి దక్షయజ్ఞే  
స త్వం ప్రభుః పశుపతిః ప్రభులక్షణోఽవ్యాః॥  
గఙ్గా ధృతా న భవతా శివ పావనీతి  
నాస్వాదితో మధుర ఇత్యపి కాలకూటః।  
సంరక్షణాయ జగతాం కరుణాతిరేకాత్  
కర్మద్వయం కలితమేతదనన్యసాధ్యమ్॥  
గఙ్గా ధృతా త్వయేశాన గఙ్గాదర్పోఽపి నాశితః।  
భగీరథానుగ్రహార్థం లోకాసమ్భేదహేతవే॥  
పురుషార్థచిన్తామణౌ---  
తస్మాదుభయత్ర ప్రదోషవ్యాప్తావవ్యాప్తౌ సామ్యేనైకదేశవ్యాప్తౌ పూర్వప్రదోషేఽధికవ్యాప్తావుత్తరప్రదోషే న్యూనవ్యాప్తావప్యుత్తరదిన ఏవ  
ప్రదోషవ్రతానుష్ఠానమితి సిద్ధమితి విభావనీయమితి దిక్।
